To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the NNLO chiral potential computed using dimensional regularization can be renormalized using generalized NN scattering lengths, but only if these are not taken to be the values extracted from high-precision potentials; that the generalized scattering lengths computed using spectral-function regularization are cutoff-independent, but that the phase shifts computed using the NNLO potential with spectral-function regularization are not.

(i) the generalized scattering lengths can be used as input for the P-wave Lippmann-Schwingerequation to renormalize the chiral NN potentials up to NNLO; (ii) the generalized scattering length extracted from the data is different than that extracted from the chiral NNLO potentials; (iii) the cutoff-dependence of the generalized scattering length and phase shifts at T lab

(1) renormalization of chiral NN potentials can be achieved by fitting to the generalized NN scattering length, (2) the generalized scattering lengths vary with cutoff and (3) the NN phase shifts at T lab � 100 Me V vary with cutoff.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a scheme that allows us to compute the P-wave phase shifts using chirally motivated NN potentials up to arbitrarily high cutoffs, and the investigation of the cutoff dependence of these observables.
the question of how much the chiral potential can be improved by using higher-order chiral effective theory corrections and/or by using different regularization methods.
the renormalization of chiral potentials, which is a necessary step for the use of chiral forces in nuclear structure calculations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chiral potentials computed with spectral-function regularization are more robust than their dimensional-regularization counterparts, but that neither is completely satisfactory.
, in the absence of a rigorous renormalization procedure, it is impossible to determine the cutoff-independent low-energy constants in the P-waves of the chiral effective field theory NN potentials.
, at NNLO, the cutoff dependence in the P-wave NN phase shifts is not under control.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in spite of the fact that chiral potentials are cutoff-independent, the NN scattering observables computed using these potentials are not.

the chiral NN potentials, computed with either dimensional regularization or spectral-function regularization, do not provide a satisfactory description of the NN data at energies above Tlab � 200 MeV.

the NNLO chiral potentials computed with dimensional regularization and spectral function regularization are not renormalization scale independent, even if the NN scattering lengths are used as input.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the renormalization of a chiral effective theory potential is not a well-defined procedure, and that the cutoff dependence in the phase shifts and scattering lengths is a manifestation of the fact that chiral effective theory is not a fundamental theory.
the cutoff dependence of the NN scattering phase shifts is not removed by using the subtractive renormalized LSE.

the NNLO chiral potentials computed using either method of regularization can be renormalized using the generalized NNLO scattering lengths as input, but the resulting NN scattering observables do not match those extracted from NN data.
